audit.reasoning: The record codes Dhao as fixed penultimate on the strength of a Wikipedia sentence, with empty quote/cite/loc/grade fields and no held file, so the verbatim check is impossible (no-held-file). Glottolog's top descriptive reference, Balukh 2020 (397-pp Leiden/LOT reference grammar), is open access; I downloaded it (423-page PDF with text layer) and read §2.3.3 'Stress Assignment' (pp. 62-64) and the related syllable sections. It states unambiguously that Dhao has fixed, non-contrastive penultimate stress, retained under prefixation and reduplication, with secondary stress on the initial syllable of four-syllable words, long vowels counted as two syllables so stress is on the penultimate vowel, and the same rule over compounds. Walker 1982 (NUSA 13, image-only; scanned of two pages at 200 dpi, one tesseract at a time) independently says 'Ndao word stress is penultimate' (§9.1.4, pp. 57-58). Bo

sources.quote: The penultimate syllable/vowel is stressed. (Every vowel constitutes a syllable.)

sources.citation: Balukh, Jermy Immanuel. 2020. A Grammar of Dhao: An Endangered Austronesian Language in Eastern Indonesia. PhD dissertation, Leiden University. LOT Dissertation Series 570. Amsterdam: LOT. xxvi+397 pp.
sources.quote: p.62: "Dhao has fixed stress, which is on penultimate syllables. Stress placement does not distinguish meaning, therefore, it is not necessary to mark stress in the orthography. As mentioned previously, stress is predictable on the penultimate syllable (see Walker, 1982; Grimes, 2010)." p.63: "The analysis above confirms that Dhao has fixed stress. Stress is not contrastive. Disyllabic roots have stress on the first syllable which is retained when roots take prefixes ... For trisyllabic roots, the main stress falls on the penultimate syllable and is retained when prefixed with pa-, as in [maˈm
sources.locator: §2.3.3 'Stress Assignment', printed pp. 62-64 (PDF pp. 88-90); also §2.1 p. 27 (PDF 53), §2.3.1 pp. 55-61, §2.2.3.8 p. 53, ch. 5 p. 179 (PDF 205), Summary p. 386 (PDF 412)
sources.note: The only reference grammar of Dhao, with a dedicated stress section (§2.3.3, pp. 62-64); our record cites Wikipedia's paraphrase of it with no grade or locator.
